desc:
For a non-empty contiguous subarray, look at the absolute value of its sum. Return the largest such absolute value over all non-empty subarrays of nums.

Examples: [1, -3, 2, 3, -4] gives 5 (the subarray [2, 3]); [-5, 2, -4] gives 7 (the whole array, sum -7).
hints: The absolute value of a sum is large when the sum is very positive or very negative. Solve the two cases separately.
The largest positive sum is classic Kadane. The most negative sum is the same idea with min instead of max.
Alternatively use prefix sums (including the empty prefix 0): a subarray sum is P[j] - P[i], so the answer is max(P) - min(P).
editorial: Run Kadane twice: once tracking the maximum sum of a subarray ending at each index, once tracking the minimum. The answer is max(maxSum, -minSum).

A neater view uses prefix sums P[0] = 0, P[k] = nums[0] + ... + nums[k-1]. Every subarray sum equals P[j] - P[i] with i < j, so the largest absolute value is the gap between the largest and the smallest prefix sum. If both extremes sit at the same position then all prefixes are equal, every element is 0 and the answer 0 is still right. One pass, O(n) time, O(1) space.
